mainTopic: Blood brought into the היכל: רבי עקיבא's source, the two-cups משנה, and the debate over קל וחומר versus the פסוק
overview: The amud opens by explaining why the משנה did not suggest placing mixed blood inside first and then outside. That fix would not work for every קרבן, because a חטאת (and, for רבי אליעזר, an אשם) becomes פסול once its blood goes inside. The גמרא then looks for the source of רבי עקיבא's rule that the blood of all קדשים becomes פסול if it is brought into the היכל. שמואל explains it with a משל about a student mixing a drink. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rejects that reading and says the source is the extra words 'כל' and 'וכל' in front of 'חטאת'. A ברייתא shows רבי יוסי הגלילי using those same words only for other kinds of חטאת, and the גמרא explains that he was only arguing according to רבי עקיבא's approach. A new משנה then covers blood split into two cups, the question of when blood brought inside becomes פסול, and the limits of the ציץ. The גמרא brings the ברייתא where רבי יוסי הגלילי and the חכמים trade קל וחומר arguments and answers from the פסוק 'אשר יובא מדמה'. It ends by starting to explain, from 'ביום השלישי', why intent to bring blood inside does not disqualify, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why not place the blood inside first, then outside?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not offer another fix: place the mixed blood inside first, and then place it outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the כהן place blood inside first, and after that place blood outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה did not suggest a simple fix for blood that is meant for inside mixed with blood meant for outside. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה itself rules that if the כהן placed inside first and then outside, the חכמים hold the outside placement is כשר. So the משנה could have told the כהן to do the inside placement first and then the outside one. The question is why it left this option out.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside, meaning in the היכל, the inner sanctuary
Outside, meaning on the outer מזבח
And then, and after that

phrases.english: And let him place [blood] inside first
phrases.notes: This is talking about a mixture of blood for the inside מזבח and blood for the outside מזבח.

phrases.english: and then place [blood] outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִיתֵּיב לְפָנִים וַהֲדַר נִיתֵּיב לַחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of how to handle mixed inside and outside blood
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's choice not to mention the inside-then-outside option
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the חכמים allow outside blood to be placed after it went inside, the משנה could have offered this easy fix

steps.title: It would not work for every offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה left it out because חטאת and אשם become פסול once their blood goes inside, so the fix could not be taught as a blanket rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there are a חטאת and an אשם, whose blood becomes פסול when it enters inside, the תנא could not state it as a rule for every case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this fix does not work for every קרבן, so the משנה did not teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the חכמים agree that a חטאת's blood becomes פסול if it is brought inside, and according to רבי אליעזר the same is true of an אשם. So 'inside first, then outside' only works for some קרבנות. A משנה prefers to teach a rule that holds across the board.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin offering
Guilt offering
Disqualified
He could not state it as a blanket rule

phrases.english: Since there are a sin offering and a guilt offering
which, when their blood enters [inside], are disqualified
it is not a blanket rule for him
phrases.notes: He means the תנא could not teach it as a rule that works for every קרבן, so he left it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא חַטָּאת וְאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: The rule is not universal (לא פסיקא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should have offered the inside-then-outside fix
steps.terutzMaskana: The fix fails for חטאת and אשם, so the משנה could not teach it as a general rule
steps.whatToRemember: A משנה often leaves out a solution that does not work for every case. Here the reason is that חטאת and אשם blood becomes פסול once it goes inside.

steps.title: שמואל's parable of the student mixing a drink
steps.stepSummary: Quoting רבי עקיבא's rule from the משנה, שמואל brings a משל: a teacher who says 'mix for me' while hot water is already being used means any kind of drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'For רבי עקיבא would say, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What is this like? A student mixed wine with hot water for his teacher. The teacher said: 'Mix for me.' The student asked: 'With what?' The teacher answered: 'Aren't we already dealing with hot water? I mean either hot or cold.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי עקיבא's rule that any outside blood brought inside becomes פסול. שמואל gives a parable to set up how this rule comes from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the משל is that repeating an obvious word is a hint. Hot water was already in use, so the teacher had no reason to say 'mix' unless he meant something wider: hot or cold. The next step applies this to the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A parable: what is this like?
Mixed (wine with water)
Hot water
Cold water

phrases.english: For Rabbi Akiva would say, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the משנה: outside blood that was brought inside to atone becomes פסול.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said
A parable: to what is this matter comparable?
To a student who mixed [wine] with hot water for his teacher
And [the teacher] said to him: Mix for me
He said to him: With what?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא בְּחַמִּין אָנוּ עֲסוּקִין עַכְשָׁיו?!
phrases.english: He said to him: Aren't we dealing with hot water now?!
[I mean] either with hot or with cold

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מָשָׁל לְמָה הַדָּבָר דּוֹמֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the source for רבי עקיבא's rule in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating something already obvious is a sign that it is meant to widen the rule

steps.title: Applying the parable: the word חטאת includes all offerings
steps.stepSummary: The parsha is already about חטאת, so writing 'חטאת' again comes to include all קדשים in the rule about blood going inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: we have already been talking about a חטאת, so why does the Torah write 'חטאת' again? Rather, it means: I am not saying this only about a חטאת, but about all קדשים.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל applies the משל to the פסוק about blood brought inside, and concludes that the rule covers all קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The parsha already talks about חטאת, so the word 'חטאת' in this פסוק seems extra. Like the teacher's extra request, the extra word widens the rule. This is רבי עקיבא's source that the blood of any קרבן becomes פסול if it is brought inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too
Since, after all
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
All sacrificial offerings

phrases.english: Here too
since we have been dealing with a sin offering all along
why do I need 'sin offering' that the Merciful One wrote?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:23

phrases.english: Rather, I am not saying it only about a sin offering
but about all sacrificial offerings

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי מִכְּדִי בְּחַטָּאת עָסְקִינַן וְאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משל from step 3 to the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra word 'חטאת' teaches that the blood of all קדשים becomes פסול if it is brought inside
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives רבי עקיבא's rule in the משנה a source in the פסוק.

steps.title: רב הונא: the extra word should limit the rule instead
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע argues the opposite: the parsha already covers all קדשים, so writing 'חטאת' must limit this rule to חטאת only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע challenged this: All קדשים are already included in this parsha for מריקה and שטיפה at the מזבח. So why does the Torah write 'חטאת' here? Learn from it: a חטאת, yes; anything else, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע attacks שמואל's reading. He uses the same 'why write חטאת?' question but reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of מריקה and שטיפה in this parsha already applies to all קדשים, so the parsha is already about every קרבן. If so, writing 'חטאת' here is not widening anything, because it is already wide. It must be narrowing the rule, so only a חטאת whose blood went inside is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it
Were included
Scouring and rinsing (of a pot used for קדשים)
Learn from it

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, challenged it
Since all sacrificial offerings were included
for the altar, regarding scouring and rinsing
phrases.notes: The פסוק about scouring and rinsing the pot (ויקרא 6:21) is in this same parsha, and it is applied to all קדשים.

phrases.english: why do I need 'sin offering' that the Merciful One wrote?
Learn from it: a sin offering, yes
anything else, no

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 4 by flipping its logic
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that the word 'חטאת' includes all קדשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parsha already includes all קדשים, so repeating 'חטאת' should narrow the rule, not widen it
steps.confusionAlert: Both שמואל and רב הונא ask the same question: why write 'חטאת'? They disagree on what the parsha is about to begin with. If it is only about חטאת, the extra word widens the rule. If it is already about all קדשים, the extra word narrows it.
steps.whatToRemember: The same 'extra word' can widen or narrow a rule. It depends on whether the parsha was already about all קדשים.

steps.title: A different parable that points the other way
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rejects שמואל's משל. He says the case is like a student who served hot and cold, and the teacher told him: only hot. That kind of instruction limits instead of widening.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is really like a student who mixed drinks for his teacher with both hot and cold water. Then the teacher told him: mix for me only with hot.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his attack on שמואל by giving a parable that fits the case better. In his parable, the teacher's words narrow things down instead of opening them up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's משל, hot water was already in use, so 'mix for me' meant any drink. In רב הונא's משל, both hot and cold were in use, so naming 'hot' cuts out the cold. In the same way, the פרשה already covers all קדשים, so naming 'חטאת' should cut the rule down to חטאת alone.

keyTerms.meaning: A student
Mixed a drink (wine with water)
Hot water
Cold water

phrases.english: And this is comparable only to a student
phrases.notes: This is still רב הונא talking. He is answering שמואל's parable from before.

phrases.english: who mixed a drink for his teacher
with both hot and cold water,
and the teacher said to him: Do not mix for me
anything but hot!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא דָּמְיָא אֶלָּא לְתַלְמִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא's objection by replacing שמואל's משל with one that supports limiting the rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: שמואל's משל of the teacher and the hot water
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פרשה already covers all קדשים, so the case is like both hot and cold being in use. Naming one item then narrows the rule instead of widening it.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's real source: the extra words 'and any'
steps.stepSummary: Since the word 'חטאת' alone cannot be the source, רב הונא says רבי עקיבא learns his rule from the fact that the פסוק says 'וכל חטאת' and not just 'חטאת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי עקיבא's reason comes from this: the פסוק does not just say 'חטאת', it says 'and any חטאת'.
steps.whatsHappening: Having knocked down שמואל's source, רב הונא now offers a new source for רבי עקיבא's rule. This line sets up the ברייתא that comes next as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is no longer the word 'חטאת' itself. Now it is the extra words 'כל' (any) and 'ו' (and) that come in front of it. Those extra words are what include other קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason or source
'And any sin offering' (ויקרא 6:23)

phrases.english: Rather, the reason of Rabbi Akiva
comes from 'sin offering' versus 'and any sin offering';

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting שמואל's reasoning, gives a new textual source for רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source for the same ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא learned his rule from the repeated word 'חטאת', as שמואל explained.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא learns it from the extra words 'כל' and 'וכל' in front of 'חטאת'.

steps.title: The ברייתא: רבי עקיבא includes all קדשים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי עקיבא reading the פסוק step by step. 'חטאת' teaches only חטאת, 'כל חטאת' adds קדשי קדשים, and 'וכל חטאת' adds קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'חטאת' gives me only a חטאת. Where do we learn קדשי קדשים? From 'כל חטאת'. Where do we learn קדשים קלים? From 'וכל חטאת'. These are רבי עקיבא's words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי עקיבא really learns from the extra words. Each extra word adds another group of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא works in levels. The plain word covers חטאת, 'כל' widens it to the other most-holy קרבנות, and the extra 'ו' widens it further to the lighter קרבנות. This backs up exactly what רב הונא said in the step before.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy קרבנות (like עולה and אשם)
קרבנות of lighter holiness (like שלמים)
'The פסוק teaches', meaning a word in the פסוק gives the answer
From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: 'Sin offering' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:23

phrases.english: I have only a sin offering;
from where do we learn offerings of the most sacred order?
The verse teaches: 'Any sin offering.'
From where do we learn offerings of lesser sanctity?
The verse teaches: 'And any sin offering.'
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the source given in step 7 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא learns the rule for all קדשים from 'כל' and 'וכל'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 6:23 word by word

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: the פסוק covers only חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees. The פסוק is only about חטאת, and the extra words add other kinds of חטאת: a communal one, and a female one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי said to him: Even if you add things all day long, I will not listen to you; the פסוק means only a חטאת. 'חטאת' gives me only a private person's חטאת. Where do we learn a communal חטאת? From 'כל חטאת'. It still gives me only a male חטאת. Where do we learn a female חטאת? From 'וכל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי הגלילי, who uses the same extra words in a different way. For him, they stay inside the world of חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that 'כל' and 'וכל' are extra and teach something. They argue about what they add. רבי עקיבא adds other kinds of קרבנות, while רבי יוסי הגלילי adds other kinds of חטאת: communal instead of private, female instead of male.

keyTerms.meaning: Includes or adds more cases from an extra word
A חטאת brought by one person
A חטאת brought for the whole community
Male / female animal

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the very same words 'כל' and 'וכל'. They are not arguing about whether these words teach something. They argue only about how far the words reach: other קרבנות, or just other kinds of חטאת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אַתָּה מְרַבֶּה כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ,
phrases.english: Even if you include more cases all day long,
I will not listen to you; it is only a sin offering.
I have only the sin offering of an individual;
from where do we learn a communal sin offering?
The verse teaches: 'Any sin offering.'
And I have only a male sin offering;
from where do we learn a female sin offering?
The verse teaches: 'And any.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא presents a תנא who disagrees with רבי עקיבא and reads the same words differently.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule about blood brought inside applies only to חטאת. 'כל' adds a communal חטאת, and 'וכל' adds another type of חטאת.

steps.title: Isn't that backwards?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא treats a male חטאת as the obvious case and a female one as the added case. A private person's normal חטאת is a female animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it the other way around?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the order in רבי יוסי הגלילי's steps. This short question sets up the fix in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain word 'חטאת' should cover the usual case. The usual private חטאת is a female animal, so the female should be the starting point, and the male should be the one that needs an extra word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Toward which side?', meaning: isn't it the opposite?

phrases.english: Isn't it the opposite?
phrases.notes: The point is that a regular private חטאת is a female animal, so the female is the obvious case, not the male.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלַפֵּי לְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the order of the cases in רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the plain word covers a male חטאת and 'וכל' adds a female one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The standard חטאת of a private person is female, so the female is the basic case and should not need an extra word.

steps.title: Fixing the order: female first, then male
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording. The plain word covers a female חטאת, and 'וכל חטאת' adds a male חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: 'חטאת' gives me only a female חטאת. Where do we learn a male חטאת? From 'וכל חטאת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question by flipping the order in the ברייתא. Now the female is the basic case and the male is the added one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing changes in רבי יוסי הגלילי's main idea: the rule stays limited to חטאת. Only the order of male and female is fixed, so the extra word adds the unusual case, a male חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he means', used to correct the wording

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא uses 'כל' and 'וכל' to bring all קדשים into the rule of blood brought inside. In his debate with רבי עקיבא, רבי יוסי הגלילי reads them as adding only other kinds of חטאת: communal, and male. Step 15 shows this was only according to רבי עקיבא's approach.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
I have only a female sin offering;
from where do we learn a male sin offering?
The verse teaches: 'And any sin offering.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10 by reversing the order of male and female.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Male חטאת is the basic case and 'וכל' adds the female.
steps.terutzMaskana: Female חטאת is the basic case and 'וכל חטאת' adds the male.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי seems to read the verse differently elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוסי הגלילי can use this פסוק to teach about a חטאת brought inside. A ברייתא quotes him saying the whole פסוק is only about פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי הגלילי really think this פסוק comes to teach this? But a ברייתא says that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds the whole passage speaks only about the bulls and goats that are burned. It teaches that their disqualified ones are burned in the Temple, and it adds a prohibition against eating them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what רבי יוסי הגלילי said in the previous steps. It quotes another ברייתא where he explains the same פסוק in a totally different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 9, רבי יוסי הגלילי read 'וכל חטאת' as being about a regular חטאת whose blood was brought inside, and said the extra words add more kinds of חטאת. In this ברייתא he says the פסוק is not about a regular חטאת at all. It is about the special פרים הנשרפים and שעירים הנשרפים, whose blood is supposed to go inside, and it teaches what to do with them when they become פסול. So it looks like he is contradicting himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Bulls that are burned: special חטאת offerings whose blood is brought inside the היכל and whose bodies are burned
Goats that are burned: the same idea as the bulls, but with goats
The Temple area
A negative commandment, a prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוסי הגלילי is saying a regular חטאת brought inside is fine to eat. The question here is only which פסוק teaches the law. In the next steps he gives a different source for it.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei HaGelili hold
that this verse comes for this purpose?!
phrases.notes: The verse is ויקרא 6:23, 'וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה', the one he was explaining in step 9.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
(Since we have found) the entire matter
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. Either way, the point is about the whole passage.

phrases.english: speaks only
about bulls that are burned and goats that are burned –
to burn their disqualified ones in the Temple,
and to establish a prohibition against eating it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי: הַאי קְרָא לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא?! וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the פסוק in step 9, using a contradicting ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of 'וכל חטאת' as being about a regular חטאת whose blood entered inside
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes him saying the פסוק is only about פרים ושעירים הנשרפים, so he cannot also use it for a regular חטאת.

steps.title: The Sages ask for the source for a regular sin offering brought inside
steps.stepSummary: Inside the same ברייתא, the חכמים ask רבי יוסי הגלילי: if the פסוק is only about the burned bulls and goats, where do we learn that a regular חטאת whose blood went inside must be burned?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: A חטאת whose blood entered the innermost place, where do we learn its law from?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. The חכמים ask רבי יוסי הגלילי a natural question that his reading raises, and he answers it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he took the פסוק away from the regular חטאת, he now needs a different source for that case. This question and his answer in the next step show that he really does not use 'וכל חטאת' for a regular חטאת, which makes the challenge from step 12 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: The innermost place, the קודש הקדשים
From where do we learn it? A request for a source.

phrases.english: They said to him:
A sin offering whose blood entered
the innermost place – from where do we learn it?
phrases.notes: He means a regular חטאת, whose blood belongs outside, that was brought inside. The question is how we know it must be burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: חַטָּאת שֶׁנִּכְנַס דָּמָהּ לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים – מִנַּיִן?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a regular חטאת whose blood went inside must be burned, according to רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: He learns it from 'Behold, its blood was not brought'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי answers that he learns it from the פסוק 'הן לא הובא את דמה', which is a different פסוק altogether.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: from the words 'Behold, its blood was not brought.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי answers the חכמים by pointing to a different פסוק. This is the end of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story of the eighth day of the מילואים, משה told אלעזר and איתמר that since the blood was not brought inside, the חטאת should have been eaten. That implies that if the blood had gone inside, it would have had to be burned. So רבי יוסי הגלילי clearly does not need 'וכל חטאת' for this law, and the contradiction with step 9 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Behold, its blood was not brought.' The פסוק he learns the law from.

phrases.english: He said to them:
"Behold, it was not brought."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: הֵן לֹא הוּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's answer to the חכמים' question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The law of a regular חטאת brought inside is learned from 'הן לא הובא את דמה'.

steps.title: He was speaking according to רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי does not really read the פסוק as being about a regular חטאת. He was only telling רבי עקיבא: even according to your reading, the פסוק covers only kinds of חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction from step 12. In his argument with רבי עקיבא, רבי יוסי הגלילי was arguing inside רבי עקיבא's own approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His own view is the one in the ברייתא: the פסוק is about פרים ושעירים הנשרפים. But he told רבי עקיבא that even if you read the פסוק as being about offerings whose blood went inside, the extra words only add more kinds of חטאת, not other קדשים. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words of someone else: arguing inside the other person's view, even if it is not your own

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי's own view is that 'וכל חטאת' is about פרים ושעירים הנשרפים, and he learns the law of a regular חטאת brought inside from 'הן לא הובא'. His argument with רבי עקיבא was only 'according to your reading'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a תנא may argue with another תנא using the other one's approach, without agreeing with it.

phrases.english: He was speaking according to the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 12-14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the earlier statement as argued inside the other side's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי הגלילי himself reads 'וכל חטאת' as being about a regular חטאת whose blood went inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only said that according to רבי עקיבא. His own view is that the פסוק is about פרים ושעירים הנשרפים.

steps.title: Blood split into two cups: one goes out, or one goes in
steps.stepSummary: A חטאת's blood was collected in two cups. If one cup left the עזרה, the other cup is כשר. If one cup entered the היכל, רבי יוסי הגלילי says the cup left outside is כשר, and the חכמים say it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חטאת whose blood was caught in two cups: if one cup went out of the עזרה, the cup still inside is כשר. If one cup went into the היכל, רבי יוסי הגלילי says the cup left outside in the עזרה is כשר, and the חכמים say it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה starts. It gives two cases where only part of a חטאת's blood went to the wrong place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one cup leaves the עזרה, everyone agrees the other cup is still good. When one cup goes into the היכל, there is a מחלוקת. The חכמים hold that the cup that went in also ruins the cup left outside, and רבי יוסי הגלילי holds it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מתניתין: our משנה
A cup used to catch the animal's blood
Outside the עזרה (the Temple courtyard)
Inside the היכל (the inner Sanctuary building)
Rules it כשר (fit to use)
Rule it פסול (unfit)

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'inner' and 'outer' change meaning between the two cases. In the first case, 'inner' (הפנימי) is the cup still in the עזרה. In the second case, 'outer' (החיצון) is that same kind of cup, the one left in the עזרה instead of going into the היכל.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ חַטָּאת שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָה בִּשְׁנֵי כּוֹסוֹת
phrases.english: MISHNA: A sin offering whose blood he collected in two cups
if one of them went outside
phrases.notes: Outside here means out of the עזרה, the Temple courtyard.

phrases.english: the inner one is fit
if one of them entered inside
phrases.notes: Inside here means into the היכל, the building past the courtyard.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili deems the outer one fit
phrases.notes: The 'outer' cup is the one that stayed out in the courtyard.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis deem it unfit

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חַטָּאת שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָה בִּשְׁנֵי כּוֹסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the previous discussion about חטאת blood brought inside ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If one cup goes out, the other cup is כשר. If one cup goes into the היכל, the cup left outside is a מחלוקת: רבי יוסי הגלילי says כשר, and the חכמים say פסול.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי's קל וחומר for his view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי argues: a wrong intent about 'outside' can ruin a קרבן, yet blood actually going outside does not ruin the leftover cup. So 'inside', where wrong intent does not ruin, surely should not ruin the leftover cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי said: Think about 'outside'. There, even a wrong intent makes the קרבן פסול, and still the cup that stayed behind is not treated like the one that went out. Now think about 'inside', where a wrong intent does not make the קרבן פסול. Isn't it logical that we should not treat the cup that stayed behind like the one that went in?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי proves his opinion from the משנה's first case using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going 'outside' is the stronger problem, because even planning to put the blood there ruins the קרבן. If that stronger problem does not spread to the leftover cup, the weaker problem of 'inside' should not spread either. So the cup left in the עזרה stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent: what the כהן plans while doing the עבודה
The leftover: here, the cup of blood that stayed behind
Isn't it logical? The opening of the conclusion of a קל וחומר
An argument from a stronger case to a weaker one

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי הגלילי builds his position on the משנה's first case, which everyone agrees to.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili said

phrases.aramaic: מָה אִם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהַמַּחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת בַּחוּץ
phrases.english: Just as in a place where intent disqualifies, outside
phrases.notes: Planning to put the blood outside the courtyard ruins the קרבן, but planning to put it inside does not.

phrases.english: it did not make the leftover blood like the blood that went out
then in a place where intent does not disqualify, inside

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשֶׂה אֶת הַמְשׁוּיָּר כַּנִּכְנָס?!
phrases.english: is it not logical that we will not make the leftover blood like the blood that went in?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי: מָה אִם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁהַמַּחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת בַּחוּץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion in the case of the two cups.
steps.raayaObject: That the cup left in the עזרה stays כשר when the other cup went into the היכל
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the agreed case of a cup that went out, where wrong intent is even stronger

steps.title: When does blood brought into the היכל become פסול?
steps.stepSummary: If the blood was brought into the היכל to do כפרה, רבי אליעזר says it is פסול even if no כפרה was done. רבי שמעון says it is only פסול once he does the כפרה there. רבי יהודה says that if he brought it in by mistake, it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the blood went into the היכל in order to do כפרה, it is פסול even though he did not do the כפרה. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי שמעון says it is not פסול until he actually does the כפרה. רבי יהודה says that if he brought it in by mistake, it is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now asks what exactly makes blood that went into the היכל become פסול, and gives three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that bringing the blood in with the plan to do כפרה is enough to ruin it. רבי שמעון holds that the blood has to actually be sprinkled inside. רבי יהודה adds that a mistaken bringing-in does not ruin the blood at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To do כפרה (atonement), meaning to sprinkle the blood
Not until he actually does the כפרה
By mistake, without meaning to

phrases.english: If it entered in order to atone
phrases.notes: The משנה means all the blood of a חטאת that belongs on the outer מזבח was brought into the היכל.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כִּפֵּר – פָּסוּל
phrases.english: even though he did not atone, it is unfit
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer
Rabbi Shimon says: not until he atones

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אִם הִכְנִיס שׁוֹגֵג – כָּשֵׁר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: if he brought it in by mistake, it is fit

steps.triggerLanguage: נִכְנַס לְכַפֵּר, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא כִּפֵּר – פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from part of the blood going in to the question of what point makes blood that went in become פסול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: פסול once it enters to do כפרה. רבי שמעון: only once he actually does the כפרה. רבי יהודה: if it was brought in by mistake, it is כשר.

steps.title: The ציץ fixes only טומאה, not blood that left
steps.stepSummary: If פסול blood was put on the מזבח, the ציץ only makes the קרבן accepted when the problem was טומאה. It does not help for blood that went out of the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With all kinds of פסול blood that was put on the מזבח, the ציץ only makes the קרבן accepted when the problem was that it was טמא. The reason is that the ציץ makes a טמא קרבן accepted, but it does not make accepted a קרבן whose blood went out.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a rule about the ציץ: what it can and cannot fix after פסול blood has already been put on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally פסול blood put on the מזבח does not count. The ציץ is an exception, but only for טומאה. Blood that went out of the עזרה is not fixed by the ציץ, so that קרבן stays unaccepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead
Makes the קרבן accepted (counted as done)
A קרבן that became טמא (ritually impure)
Blood or meat that went out of the עזרה
On top of the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The ציץ is a narrow fix. It saves a קרבן that became טמא, but it does not save blood that left the עזרה or was ruined in other ways.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַדָּמִים פְּסוּלִין שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
phrases.english: All the unfit blood that he placed on the altar

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִרְצָה הַצִּיץ אֶלָּא עַל הַטָּמֵא
phrases.english: the frontplate effects acceptance only for the impure
for the frontplate effects acceptance for the impure
but does not effect acceptance for what went out
phrases.notes: He means blood or meat that left the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הַדָּמִים פְּסוּלִין שֶׁנְּתָנוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing rule about what happens after פסול blood has already been put on the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ציץ makes a קרבן accepted only when the problem is טומאה, not when the blood went out of the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי's logical argument that inside blood does not ruin the outside cup
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's קל וחומר: if blood leaving the עזרה, where wrong intent ruins, does not ruin the cup left behind, then blood entering the היכל, where wrong intent does not ruin, surely does not ruin the cup left behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: A ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי הגלילי said, here is a קל וחומר. Outside the עזרה is a place where a wrong intent can ruin a קרבן. Even so, blood that went outside does not ruin the blood still inside. Inside the היכל is a place where a wrong intent does not ruin. So surely blood that went inside should not ruin the blood still outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that spells out the reasoning behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's opinion in the משנה. He builds a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Outside' (out of the עזרה) is the stricter place, because even a wrong intent about it ruins a קרבן. Yet the משנה agrees that blood actually going outside does not ruin the leftover cup. So 'inside' (the היכל), the more lenient place, should certainly not ruin the leftover cup.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
A wrong intent makes the קרבן פסול
Outside, here meaning outside the עזרה
Inside, here meaning inside the היכל

phrases.english: GEMARA: It is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, קַל וָחוֹמֶר:
phrases.english: רבי יוסי הגלילי said: it is a קל וחומר:
Just as in a place where intent disqualifies, outside,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' here means outside the עזרה. Planning to do the עבודה out there ruins a קרבן.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא פָּסַל דָּם שֶׁבַּחוּץ אֶת שֶׁבִּפְנִים;
phrases.english: the blood outside does not disqualify the blood inside;
then in a place where intent does not disqualify, inside,
phrases.notes: 'Inside' here means inside the היכל.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it will not disqualify:
the blood inside will not disqualify the blood outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא אמר רבי יוסי הגלילי קל וחומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא source behind רבי יוסי הגלילי's reasoning in the משנה (step 17).
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי הגלילי's ruling that the cup left outside stays כשר when the other cup entered the היכל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר comparing 'outside the עזרה' (where intent ruins) with 'inside the היכל' (where intent does not ruin).

steps.title: The חכמים answer from the פסוק: even part of the blood
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the קל וחומר. The פסוק says 'אשר יובא מדמה', which teaches that even part of the blood entering the היכל makes the חטאת פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But the פסוק says 'whereof any of its blood is brought.' That means even if only part of its blood went in.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי הגלילי's logic with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר cannot stand against a clear פסוק. The word 'מדמה' (from its blood) shows that even some of the blood going into the היכל ruins the whole חטאת, including the cup left outside.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whereof any of its blood is brought' (into the היכל)
Part of its blood

phrases.english: They said to him: But it says:
"whereof any of its blood is brought"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:23

phrases.english: even part of its blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרו לו הרי הוא אומר אשר יובא מדמה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 20 by pointing to a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole conclusion of רבי יוסי הגלילי's קל וחומר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק explicitly makes even part of the blood entering the היכל ruin the חטאת, so logic cannot override it.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי turns the logic around against the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי answers: if blood entering the lenient place (the היכל) ruins the leftover cup, then blood leaving to the strict place (outside the עזרה) should surely ruin the leftover cup too. Yet everyone agrees it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: then from now on there is a קל וחומר about blood that leaves. Inside the היכל, wrong intent does not ruin, and still blood that went inside ruins the blood left outside. Outside the עזרה, wrong intent does ruin. So surely blood that went outside should ruin the blood left inside!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי הגלילי challenges the חכמים by showing that their reading leads to a result nobody accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you accept that 'inside' ruins the leftover cup, then 'outside', the stricter place, should ruin even more. But the משנה says that when one cup leaves the עזרה, the other cup is כשר. So the חכמים's reading seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: About the blood that leaves (the עזרה)
From now on, meaning 'if you say so'
Is it not logical?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם, קַל וָחוֹמֶר לַיּוֹצֵא מֵעַתָּה:
phrases.english: He said to them: from now there is a קל וחומר for blood that leaves:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין מַחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת, בִּפְנִים –
phrases.english: Just as in a place where intent does not disqualify, inside,
the blood inside disqualifies the blood outside;
phrases.notes: Here 'outside' means outside the היכל, still in the עזרה, where the second cup was left.

phrases.english: then in a place where intent disqualifies, outside,
is it not logical that it will disqualify:
the blood outside will disqualify the blood inside?

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר להם קל וחומר ליוצא מעתה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the חכמים's reading of the פסוק (step 21) with a reverse קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's ruling that blood entering the היכל ruins the leftover cup.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If entering the lenient place ruins, then leaving to the stricter place should ruin too. That contradicts the agreed rule that the remaining cup is כשר when one cup leaves the עזרה.

steps.title: The חכמים answer: only blood that enters ruins
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the פסוק says 'יובא', 'is brought in'. So only blood that enters the היכל ruins the leftover cup. Blood that leaves the עזרה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But the פסוק says 'is brought in.' Blood that enters ruins the rest, and blood that leaves does not ruin the rest.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יוסי הגלילי's reverse קל וחומר by pointing again to the wording of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'יובא' limits the rule to blood brought into the היכל. Since the פסוק itself sets this limit, there is no room for a קל וחומר to extend it to blood that leaves the עזרה. This ends the ברייתא's debate.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood that enters (the היכל)
The blood that leaves (the עזרה)
Makes פסול

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the פסוק 'אשר יובא מדמה' teaches two things: even part of the blood entering the היכל ruins the חטאת, and only entering ruins, not leaving the עזרה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר ״אֲשֶׁר יוּבָא״ –
phrases.english: They said to him: But it says "is brought":
phrases.notes: The same פסוק as before, ויקרא 6:23. This time the focus is on the word 'brought in'.

phrases.english: what enters disqualifies,
and what leaves does not disqualify.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמרו לו הרי הוא אומר אשר יובא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the reverse קל וחומר of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק's wording ('יובא' means only entering).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since entering the היכל ruins, leaving the עזרה, a stricter place, should ruin even more.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק restricts the rule to blood that enters, so blood that leaves does not ruin the remaining cup.

steps.title: Should intent to bring blood inside also disqualify?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes a קל וחומר: if מחשבה about outside disqualifies, even though blood that went outside does not ruin the rest, then מחשבה about inside should surely disqualify, since blood that went inside does ruin the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let intent to bring the blood inside the היכל disqualify the קרבן, based on a קל וחומר. Outside the עזרה, blood that went out does not ruin the blood still inside, and yet intent about outside does disqualify. Inside the היכל, blood that went in does ruin the blood still outside. So is it not logical that intent about inside should disqualify too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses what it just learned to build a new קל וחומר. It suggests that intent to bring the blood into the היכל should make the קרבן פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the last step we know that blood actually entering the היכל is 'stronger' than blood leaving the עזרה, because only blood entering the היכל ruins the leftover cup. Yet for intent, only outside is known to disqualify. The גמרא asks: if the 'weaker' place disqualifies through intent, shouldn't the 'stronger' place disqualify through intent even more?

keyTerms.meaning: Intent: what the כהן has in mind while doing the עבודה
Inside: here, inside the היכל
Outside: here, outside the עזרה
Is it not logical: the closing phrase of a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר flips the earlier one. Before, רבי יוסי הגלילי argued that outside is the strict place. Here the strict place is inside, because blood entering the היכל is the case that ruins the leftover cup.

phrases.english: And let intent [to bring the blood] inside disqualify
based on a קל וחומר:
And just as in a place where it does not disqualify
the blood that is outside [does not disqualify] the [blood] that is inside –
phrases.notes: This is the case from step 23: blood that left the עזרה does not ruin the cup left behind.

phrases.english: intent disqualifies regarding outside,
a place where the blood that is inside disqualifies
the blood that is outside –
is it not logical
that intent should disqualify regarding inside?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְהֵא מַחְשָׁבָה בִּפְנִים פּוֹסֶלֶת מִקַּל וְחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חכמים's conclusion from step 23 (only blood entering the היכל ruins the leftover cup) as the base for a new קל וחומר about intent.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted rule that only intent about outside the עזרה disqualifies, and intent about inside the היכל does not.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: inside is stricter than outside for actual blood, since it ruins the leftover cup. So if intent about outside disqualifies, intent about inside should disqualify even more.

steps.title: The פסוק 'ביום השלישי' blocks the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to reject the קל וחומר by quoting the פסוק 'ביום השלישי', which is the source for the rules of intent. The explanation continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'On the third day' –
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by quoting a פסוק. This line sets up the next move, and the full reasoning comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules of intent come from this פסוק, not from logic. By quoting it, the גמרא signals that the פסוק limits which kinds of intent disqualify, so a קל וחומר cannot add a new one. How exactly the פסוק teaches this comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Behold, it says: introduces a פסוק that settles the question
'On the third day': from the פסוק about a קרבן eaten too late
A קרבן ruined by wrong intent. This פסוק goes on to say 'פגול הוא'

phrases.english: Behold, it says:
"On the third day" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:7. The גמרא explains how this פסוק answers the question in the lines that come next.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to reject the קל וחומר of step 24 by pointing to the פסוק that is the source for the rules of intent.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed קל וחומר that intent to bring blood into the היכל disqualifies.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rules of intent come from the פסוק 'ביום השלישי', so a קל וחומר cannot add a new kind of intent beyond what that פסוק teaches. The details continue in the next lines.
